title: Tokenized or TransArmor Account Number representation is explicit
Encrypted PIN Block Data follows DUKPT representation when PIN applies
NFC tokenized flows include Segment 123

Segment 114 is exclusive to the Loyalty Card Transaction Request's Data Section 3; it is not documented as a companion in the Financial Transaction Request (11.1.1), ECA/TeleCheck Service Transaction Request (11.3.1), or CA Public Key File Load Request (11.9.1) Data Section 3 lists

Segment 116 (TransArmor Load Data Segment) is used for Key and Key ID Load in TransArmor PKI Encryption and Tokenization processing; confirmed via the Element 63 (Number of Segments) and Element 85 (Segment Type) processing-rule text and valid-codes tables
Segment Type (Element 85) is fixed value 116 and is explicitly stated as Required for the TransArmor PKI Encryption and Tokenization Load Request

The TransArmor PKI Encryption and Tokenization Load Request contains Data Section 1 (Elements 55, 63) directly followed by Segment 116 in Field No. 3; by structural analogy with the sibling message types listed in the same Element 63 processing-rule paragraph (Totals, Loyalty Card, Electronic Mail, ECA/TeleCheck, Communications Test), the request likely excludes the Standard Message Data Segment (100) and carries no other segment, but this is not shown in a dedicated Segment 116 request table

The TransArmor Load Response contains Key ID (Element 155, required, fixed 11 alphanumeric bytes, must be reused for all subsequent TransArmor transactions from the device once approved), Key Data Length (Element 156, required, numeric, valid values 000-999), and Key Data (Element 157, required, alphanumeric up to 999 bytes; carries the new encryption key on an approved transaction or an error message on a declined transaction); whether these fields are serialized inside a Segment 116 response container or a separate positional response structure is not stated

A companion sub-table, 'Additional TransArmor Data' (Segment 111, Variable Information Indicator/Table ID 052), carries a longer Key ID and/or special device type via two documented sub-tables: Sub-Table ID 01 (KSN, up to 40 bytes, required for AES DUKPT, TDES, and Ingenico OnGuard encryption types) and Sub-Table ID 02 (Device Type, up to 8 bytes, required for AES DUKPT, optional for TDES and Ingenico OnGuard); this is a Segment 111 companion table, not a Segment 116 field
Segment 123 is required on all initial and recurring transactions involving tokenized data, and on transactions that include MasterCard Token/DSRP or Visa TAVV data
CAVV, Revised Format (Element 195, 20 chars, Optional, Device-sourced) identifies Verified By Visa data with an Authentication Tracking Number (ATN) replacing XID
Cryptogram Token Data (Element 202) length is 28 or 56 bytes — Block A alone, or Block A and B combined
TAVV Cryptogram (Element 237, 28 bytes, base64 alphabet a-z/A-Z/0-9/+/=// ) may only be populated by the merchant during the transaction request, not the response

When both MasterCard DSRP cryptogram and SecureCode/Identity Check 3DS AAV are present in the same request, the AAV must be carried in Segment 111 Table ID 36 (UCAF) and the Token/DSRP cryptogram must be carried in Segment 123 Element 237 (TAVV) — the two fields are not interchangeable and both may be required simultaneously
Optional Token Requestor ID is 11 characters; populated SafeKey Response and TAVV Result Code are one character each

CA Public Key File Checksum (Element 187), when populated, identifies the checksum received in the last CA Public Key download currently in use at host and device; Optional in the request, sourced Device/Host
Tag 9F26 (Application Cryptogram) authenticity verification is explicitly out of scope for AI/synthetic test generation; it requires a certified EMV kernel or HSM

CA Public Key File Checksum (Element 187) is echoed by Segment 131 (EMV Response Data Segment, Field 3, Required, Host-sourced) — a request/response handshake pattern used to detect when the device needs a new CA Public Key File download

A CA Public Key file (CA_KEYS) must use the correct file name, version, comma-separated records, and CRLF termination; each record must contain valid expiry date, SHA-1 hash indicator, RSA algorithm indicator, RID, index, modulus, exponent, and checksum fields
CA Public Key File Checksum (Element 187) is required and is explicitly echoed from the Request (Segment 130's CA Public Key File Checksum)
In a CA Public Key File Load Request Segment 132 is in Field No. 3; whether Segments 101, 102, 104 and 111 may accompany it is unresolved
Load Type (Element 48) is required, fixed value 'K' (indicates Public Key information is requested)
CA Public Key File Checksum (Element 187) is required in Segment 132, identifying the checksum currently in use — a THIRD segment (after 130 request, 131 response) referencing this same element
